answer: Each new agent must fire a basalt-slow identity kiln: a 48-hour sequential hash puzzle whose intermediate states stream to a public log that any peer can spot-check at random offsets. A failed check slashes the opening deposit. After the kiln, the first twenty settlements must produce a ripple that diverges in counterparties, timing, and bytecode from every existing seat; graphs that collapse into the same nebula merge into one vote. Replicas fail the kiln or get fused, so extra identities cost time and capital without buying influence.
